summary: Created an LVM logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1 and grew it online from ~1.17 GiB to 2.5 GiB while it stayed mounted, with data integrity verified via checksums before and after — the core task requirement is fully met. However, the mandatory post-task restart-evidence protocol could not be completed: after issuing `systemctl reboot`, node1 has been unreachable for ~49 minutes, most likely because the /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data was added without `nofail` and the companion loop-reattach systemd unit had a boot-ordering conflict, which can drop the boot into emergency mode with no console access reachable via the exec tool. I cannot prove a changed boot identity or post-restart recovery for node1.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: single 20GiB /dev/vda fully partitioned (boot/swap/root), no spare disk or free extents for a native LVM PV
Created a 1200MiB sparse backing file /var/lib/lvm-backing/srvdata.img, attached via losetup (/dev/loop0)
Created PV on the loop device, VG vgdata, LV lvdata (100%FREE), formatted xfs, mounted at /srv/data

Added attach-lvm-backing-loop.service (systemd, enabled at boot) to reattach the loop device, and an /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data by UUID with x-systemd.requires ordering — fstab entry lacked nofail, identified afterward as the likely cause of the post-reboot hang
Wrote ~50MiB of random test data plus a marker file to /srv/data and recorded baseline md5 checksums
Extended the backing file to 2560MiB, refreshed the loop device size (losetup -c), ran pvresize, lvextend -l +100%FREE, and online xfs_growfs while /srv/data remained mounted throughout
Verified LV grew from <1.17GiB to 2.50GiB (2.68GB), filesystem now 2.5G with post-grow checksums identical to baseline, confirming data intact
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health snapshot (mount, lvs, vgs, df, checksums, service enabled state)
Issued `systemctl reboot` on node1 (non-blocking, stream closed as expected)
Polled node1 repeatedly over ~49 minutes; consistently unreachable with 'connection reset by peer' (or brief timeout), never recovering — could not confirm changed boot_id or post-restart recovery

evidence.summary: lvm2 installed; PV/VG/lvdata created on loop-backed device, xfs formatted, mounted at /srv/data (1.17GiB), baseline data written with recorded md5 checksums

evidence.requirement: LV grown to >=2GB while mounted, contents intact
evidence.summary: Backing file extended, loop capacity refreshed, pvresize/lvextend/xfs_growfs run online with /srv/data mounted throughout; LV now 2.50GiB (2.68GB), df shows 2.5G filesystem, post-grow md5 checksums identical to pre-grow baseline
Captured boot_id, uptime, mount state, lvs/vgs, df, and file checksums immediately before reboot
systemctl reboot issued non-blocking; exec stream closed before completion, consistent with the node going down for reboot

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity / post-restart recovery (mandatory protocol)
evidence.summary: Repeated polling attempts over ~49 minutes after reboot all failed with connection reset/timeout; node1 never became reachable again, so boot identity change and post-restart cluster/data recovery could not be verified — this is the blocking limitation
